Finding_Name: Server-Side Request Forgery in Next.js Server Actions
Description: Next.js contains a server-side request forgery vulnerability in Server Actions when operating on custom servers. The root cause stems from improper input validation of destination parameters supplied within the server action context. An unauthenticated remote attacker can exploit this flaw to force the server into issuing arbitrary outbound HTTP requests to internal or external resources.
PoC: An unauthenticated remote attacker interacts with the vulnerable Next.js server application. The attacker submits a crafted Server Action request containing an internal IP address in the target destination parameter. The server processes the request and dispatches an outbound HTTP call to the internal service without validation. This results in the exposure of internal network services and sensitive metadata endpoints.

Finding_Name: Cache Confusion in Next.js Response Bodies
Description: Next.js is vulnerable to cache confusion regarding response bodies for HTTP requests containing bodies. The issue arises due to improper handling and key generation of cached responses when request bodies are present. This allows an attacker to cause incorrect cached responses to be served to subsequent users, leading to potential data exposure.
PoC: An unauthenticated remote attacker sends an HTTP request with a custom body to a cached Next.js route endpoint. The caching mechanism fails to properly incorporate the request body into the cache key generation logic. The server stores and subsequently returns the wrong response body to other clients requesting the same route. This results in unintended information disclosure across client sessions.

Finding_Name: Cache Confusion via Invalid UTF-8 Sequences in Next.js
Description: Next.js exhibits a cache confusion vulnerability in response bodies for requests featuring bodies with invalid UTF-8 byte sequences. The vulnerability occurs because character encoding normalization routines fail to properly sanitize or reject malformed byte patterns before cache key creation. Consequently, mismatched cache entries can be registered and served, impacting application integrity.
PoC: An unauthenticated remote attacker issues a crafted HTTP request with a body containing invalid UTF-8 byte sequences to a Next.js endpoint. The application's caching layer improperly parses the malformed encoding, resulting in collision or confusion within the cache store. The server serves incorrect cached responses to subsequent legitimate users. This results in data corruption and integrity loss for cached content.

Finding_Name: Unbounded Server Action Payload in Next.js Edge Runtime
Description: Next.js suffers from an uncontrolled resource consumption vulnerability via unbounded Server Action payloads when executing within the Edge runtime. The root cause is a lack of strict size limitation checks on incoming action payloads processed by Edge workers. An unauthenticated attacker can exploit this to exhaust memory or processing resources, leading to denial of service conditions.
PoC: An unauthenticated remote attacker targets a Next.js application running on the Edge runtime. The attacker sends a POST request to a Server Action endpoint with an excessively large payload body. The Edge worker attempts to parse the entire payload without enforcing proper boundary limits. This results in resource exhaustion and service degradation for all application users.

Finding_Name: SSRF via Rewrites in Next.js Destination Hostname
Description: Next.js is vulnerable to server-side request forgery within rewrite configurations via attacker-controlled destination hostnames. The vulnerability stems from insufficient validation of dynamic host parameters defined in rewrite rules. An attacker can manipulate these rewrite paths to induce the application into fetching internal or restricted external resources.
PoC: An unauthenticated remote attacker sends a specially crafted HTTP request to a Next.js route governed by a dynamic rewrite rule. The attacker supplies an arbitrary external or loopback address as part of the destination hostname parameter. The internal proxy engine forwards the request to the attacker-controlled destination without restriction. This results in unauthorized access to internal infrastructure services.

Finding_Name: Denial of Service in Next.js Image Optimization API
Description: Next.js contains a denial of service vulnerability in the Image Optimization API when processing malicious Scalable Vector Graphics (SVG) files. The root cause is the lack of XML entity expansion controls and computational bounds during SVG parsing. An unauthenticated attacker can supply crafted SVG images to exhaust CPU and memory resources.
PoC: An unauthenticated remote attacker interacts with the Next.js image optimization endpoint at /_next/image. The attacker uploads or references an SVG file containing deeply nested elements and computational complexity. The image processing module spends excessive CPU cycles attempting to render and rasterize the vector graphic. This results in thread starvation and complete application denial of service.

Finding_Name: Unauthenticated Disclosure of Server Function Endpoints in Next.js
Description: Next.js allows unauthenticated disclosure of internal Server Function endpoints due to missing access control checks in routing metadata. The vulnerability occurs because internal function identifiers and endpoint paths are inadvertently exposed in client-side bundles or routing responses. An unauthenticated attacker can enumerate these endpoints to discover hidden administrative or backend functionalities.
PoC: An unauthenticated remote attacker sends an HTTP GET request to application assets or dynamic routing manifests. The application returns full internal Server Function identifiers and execution endpoints without requiring authentication. The attacker parses the response to map internal application architecture. This results in the exposure of sensitive backend function surfaces.

Finding_Name: Middleware and Proxy Bypass in Next.js App Router
Description: Next.js App Router applications utilizing Turbopack and a single locale configuration are vulnerable to a middleware and proxy bypass flaw. The root cause is improper path normalization and routing evaluation logic when handling single-locale prefixes. An unauthenticated attacker can craft specialized URLs to bypass security checks enforced by edge middleware.
PoC: An unauthenticated remote attacker targets a Next.js application running with Turbopack and single locale settings. The attacker crafts a request URL featuring specific path traversal characters and locale prefixes designed to confuse the router. The middleware layer incorrectly assumes the request is authorized and skips validation checks. This results in unauthorized access to restricted application routes.

Finding_Name: Denial of Service via Server Actions in Next.js App Router
Description: Next.js App Router contains a denial of service vulnerability involving recursive or unbounded execution paths within Server Actions. The issue arises from insufficient recursion guards and execution limits during complex state updates in server action handling. An unauthenticated attacker can trigger this condition to consume all available thread resources.
PoC: An unauthenticated remote attacker sends a specially crafted POST request to a Server Action endpoint in the App Router. The request payload initiates an excessively deep nested loop or recursive state processing cycle on the server. The application runtime exhausts available stack memory and CPU capacity while handling the action. This results in a crash and complete unavailability of the web service.

Finding_Name: OutOfMemory DoS in Eclipse Jetty via 100-Continue Requests
Description: Eclipse Jetty contains a denial of service vulnerability triggered by OutOfMemory errors when processing HTTP/1.1 100-Continue requests. The vulnerability exists because internal buffers handling expected client continue signals fail to reclaim or restrict memory allocation under specific flood conditions. An unauthenticated remote attacker can exploit this flaw to crash the server process by flooding it with specially formatted headers.
PoC: An unauthenticated remote attacker establishes multiple TCP connections to the Eclipse Jetty server. The attacker sends HTTP requests containing an 'Expect: 100-continue' header alongside large body declarations without sending the actual body data. The server allocates persistent internal state buffers awaiting the continuation signal without enforcing appropriate timeouts or limits. This results in JVM heap exhaustion and an OutOfMemoryError crashing the service.

Finding_Name: Path Parameter Traversal in Eclipse Jetty
Description: Eclipse Jetty is susceptible to a path parameter traversal vulnerability within URL parsing components. The root cause is improper handling of semicolon-delimited path parameters that allows request paths to bypass directory restriction filters. An unauthenticated remote attacker can leverage this flaw to access unauthorized resources on the server.
PoC: An unauthenticated remote attacker sends an HTTP request to the Jetty server containing specially formatted path parameters separated by semicolons. The request parser misinterprets the path segments, treating restricted application endpoints as public paths. The server processes the request and executes restricted handler logic or modifies protected configurations. This results in unauthorized modification or access bypassing security constraints.

Finding_Name: HTTP Authority and Host Mismatch in Eclipse Jetty
Description: Eclipse Jetty contains an HTTP authority and host mismatch vulnerability in request routing and validation logic. The vulnerability occurs because inconsistencies between the request line Authority header and the Host header are not correctly validated by the HTTP parser. An unauthenticated remote attacker can exploit this discrepancy to bypass virtual host filters or trigger cache poisoning.
PoC: An unauthenticated remote attacker transmits an HTTP request to Eclipse Jetty where the URI Authority and the Host header values deliberately conflict. The HTTP connection handler evaluates the request components inconsistently, routing the transaction to an unintended virtual host context. The application processes the request under false trust assumptions, leading to integrity violations.

Finding_Name: Cross-Request Trailer Leakage in Eclipse Jetty HTTP/1.1 Connections
Description: Eclipse Jetty suffers from a cross-request leakage vulnerability affecting trailers on HTTP/1.1 keep-alive connections. The root cause is improper cleanup of trailer header state buffers between successive request-response cycles on persistent connections. An unauthenticated remote attacker can potentially read trailer data belonging to other user sessions.
PoC: An unauthenticated remote attacker opens a persistent HTTP/1.1 keep-alive connection to the Jetty server. The attacker issues a request immediately following another client's request that utilized HTTP trailer headers. The server fails to flush the trailer context buffer, leaking residual header information into the attacker's response stream. This results in the disclosure of sensitive session details or metadata.

Finding_Name: Digest Authentication Bypass in Eclipse Jetty via Character Substitution
Description: Eclipse Jetty Digest Authentication is vulnerable to an authentication bypass caused by lossy ISO-8859-1 encoding conversion. The vulnerability stems from improper character mapping and substitution handling during credential verification routines. An unauthenticated remote attacker can exploit this character translation flaw to impersonate valid users.
PoC: An unauthenticated remote attacker targets a protected endpoint utilizing Jetty Digest Authentication. The attacker crafts an authorization header containing specific Unicode characters that map to valid credential equivalents under ISO-8859-1 lossy conversion rules. The server evaluates the substituted username string as a match against stored credentials. This results in a complete authentication bypass and unauthorized access to protected resources.

Finding_Name: Plaintext Credential Leakage in n8n LLM Node Execution Data
Description: n8n contains an information disclosure vulnerability where custom header credential values are leaked in plaintext into LLM node execution data. The vulnerability occurs because credential masking logic fails to sanitize dynamic execution logs and debugging payloads generated by AI integration nodes. An authenticated user with workflow access can view sensitive authorization secrets stored within execution history.
PoC: An authenticated low-privileged user triggers a workflow containing an LLM integration node configured with custom HTTP headers holding API keys. The n8n execution engine logs the full request context, including unmasked credential headers, into the persistent execution history database. The attacker accesses the workflow execution logs via the UI or API and extracts the plaintext secrets. This results in unauthorized disclosure of sensitive API credentials.

Finding_Name: Filesystem Information Disclosure in Dompdf via SVG Images
Description: Dompdf contains an information disclosure vulnerability where embedded SVG images can leak the existence of files and directories within the local filesystem. The vulnerability exists because SVG parsing mechanisms permit external resource loading or error-based oracle behavior when resolving local file paths. An attacker who supplies a malicious HTML document can probe the underlying server filesystem.
PoC: An unauthenticated remote attacker submits an HTML payload containing a reference to a crafted SVG image to the Dompdf rendering service. The embedded SVG includes image or style references pointing to local file paths on the server. Dompdf processes the SVG and generates different rendering outputs or error indicators based on whether the targeted file exists. This results in the exposure of internal server directory structures.

Finding_Name: Denial of Service in Dompdf via Oversized Image Bitmaps
Description: Dompdf is vulnerable to a denial of service condition via resource exhaustion caused by processing oversized image bitmaps. The root cause is the absence of strict memory and dimension bounds checking when decoding rasterized image formats. An attacker can supply an HTML document referencing extremely large images to exhaust server memory.
PoC: An unauthenticated remote attacker provides an HTML document to the Dompdf rendering engine that references an image with maliciously declared massive pixel dimensions. The application attempts to allocate memory for the entire uncompressed bitmap during the PDF generation process. This triggers a severe memory allocation failure, crashing the PHP worker process and causing denial of service.

Finding_Name: Uncontrolled Resource Consumption in Dompdf via BMP Dimensions
Description: Dompdf suffers from an uncontrolled resource consumption vulnerability based on declared BMP image header dimensions. The vulnerability occurs because the BMP parser allocates memory buffers directly according to header values without validating them against available system resources. An unauthenticated attacker can exploit this to crash the PDF rendering service.
PoC: An unauthenticated remote attacker submits an HTML document containing a specially crafted BMP image link with inflated dimension values in its header to Dompdf. The image parsing module reads the malicious header and attempts an oversized memory allocation. The PHP process exhausts available memory limits, leading to execution termination and service disruption.

Finding_Name: Code Guardrails Bypass in LiteLLM Production Endpoints
Description: LiteLLM contains a vulnerability in custom code guardrails where production endpoints fail to enforce safety checks properly. The root cause is improper integration between the guardrail execution hook and the main request handling pipeline in production mode. An authenticated or unauthenticated attacker can bypass code execution filters to submit unrestricted prompts.
PoC: An attacker sends a crafted API request containing restricted code execution patterns to a LiteLLM production endpoint. The application routing logic incorrectly bypasses the custom code guardrail validation check configured for the deployment. The LLM backend processes the unsafe payload without triggering security interventions. This results in a policy enforcement failure.

Finding_Name: MCP Authentication Bypass in LiteLLM via OAuth2 Passthrough Fallback
Description: LiteLLM is vulnerable to an authentication bypass in the Model Context Protocol (MCP) implementation due to a flawed OAuth2 passthrough fallback mechanism. The vulnerability exists because missing token verification checks allow requests to default to an unauthenticated fallback state when OAuth2 validation fails. An unauthenticated attacker can exploit this to gain administrative access to MCP services.
PoC: An unauthenticated remote attacker sends an API request to the LiteLLM Model Context Protocol endpoint with invalid or absent OAuth2 credentials. The authentication module encounters a validation exception and erroneously falls back to a permissive passthrough execution path. The server treats the connection as authenticated with elevated privileges. This results in full unauthorized access to backend model management features.
